purpose: Establish PMR modification-number reading, native use, genuine clock conventions and FileMobId/MasterMobId terminology before choosing Bella DTM behavior.
scope: Read-only native arm64 instruction analysis, Avid primary documentation and filesystem/PMR-hash recheck. No production code or media changes.

native.scope: Read-only static arm64 instructions from installed Media Composer 26.8.0.58987. No private API execution, media rescans or repository edits.
conclusions: DTM is a cached per-media-file modification value used for freshness/change detection. It is not a media identity, project name, Date Created or recording date.
Current Mac ScanMXFFileToCache gets low 32 bits of stat st_mtimespec.tv_sec through GetModDateUTC. Thus this producer writes Unix modification seconds, truncated to 32 bits.
ReadPmrRec reads an unsigned 32-bit scalar with byte-order handling and caches it unchanged; it does not turn it into a calendar date or repair a historical epoch.

ScanDirectoryToCache compares cached DTM with a modification word already present in its directory-entry vector. Equal or absolute difference exactly 3600 can retain the cache entry; other differences remove stale entries and trigger scanning the file again.
CompareDirectoryToCache separately calls live GetModDateUTC and reports filenames with different values, also accepting an exact one-hour difference.

The comparison is not a checksum: equality does not prove byte-for-byte equality. Avid accepts an exact one-hour difference; its purpose may relate to clock conventions but no intent is asserted from instructions alone.
Retaining four raw bytes is distinct from enabling a filesystem comparison and using mismatch to trigger a header read. Whether Bella needs the latter is a product decision.

producer.operation: File-locator virtual +0x320 called with true; preserves returned modification value.
Calls AMacFileSystemObject::GetModDateUTC and zero-extends low 32 bits at 0xe340c.
stat(); on success ldr w19 from stat buffer+0x30 (st_mtimespec.tv_sec low32). true-on-error path supplies 0xffffffff.
Timestamp argument x6 saved as w24, stores low32 in fileInfo+0x10.
Copies fileInfo+0x10 to PMR in-memory record+0x280.
Loads record+0x280 and writes through AStream virtual+0x178, verified WriteUInt32 0x258d0.

reader.operation: AStream virtual+0x250, diagnostic label DTM; actual AStream::ReadUInt32 0x27054. Stores w0 in record+0x280.
Reads exactly four bytes, loads w0, reverses byte order if stream swap flag+0x1b6 is set.
Loads record+0x280 into w6, passes to AddCacheEntry via manager virtual+0x328. No epoch/timezone conversion.

conditions: Iterates supplied dirEntry_t vector, filtering known nonmedia names and entry kind; file cache looked up by filename.

Only existing matching cache candidates reach timestamp compare. First comparison candidate flag w21 initialized true at 0x44c704; mismatch clears it while further stale duplicate entries are removed.
No special zero-DTM validity test occurs in this comparison. Zero is compared as a number. No epoch or timezone conversion occurs between loading the two words and comparing.

instructions.operation: ldr w8,[sp,#0xb0]: cached fileInfo+0x10 timestamp, because temporary fileInfo begins at sp+0xa0.
ldur w9,[x28,#-4]: current directory entry+0x20c, because x28 points one 0x210-byte record past current entry.
Subtract 32-bit words; equality or absolute 32-bit difference 0xe10 (3600) takes retained-entry path.
Sets cached present marker at fileInfo+0x54 and replaces hash-table value, without invoking ScanFileToCache for that retained entry.
Removes stale filename hash-table entry and calls manager virtual+0x330 DeleteCacheEntry.
New or stale flag invokes manager virtual+0x2c8 ScanFileToCache.

secondaryConsumer.caller: LocalMDB::ScanDirectoryToMDB 0x416770 gets MSMDB at0x416ccc, calls actual manager+0x210 at0x416d0c; target verified 0x453604.

instructions.operation: Calls file locator GetModDateUTC(false), saves live value in x27.
If changed-output AArray is null, no change report is produced.
Loads cached fileInfo+0x10 as unsigned32, subtracts from live value, accepts equality or exact absolute difference3600.
Appends filename to changed-output array when values differ otherwise.

operations: Non-Unity branch uses FSGetCatalogInfoBulk at0x1837c, calls UTCToLocalTime at0x184ac, stores output into entry+0x20c at0x184b0.
Unity branch uses stat at0x18754, calls UTCToLocalTime at0x187f8, stores output into entry+0x20c at0x187fc.
UTCToLocalTime0x4e0f0 calls UCConvertSecondsToCFAbsoluteTime, CFTimeZoneCopySystem, CFTimeZoneGetSecondsFromGMT and UCConvertCFAbsoluteTimeToSeconds, then adds zone offset.
directoryEntryQualification.limit: Do not describe every directory-entry consumer as a normalized Unix UTC comparison. The precise source clock convention of the supplied directory-entry vector is separate from the raw comparison. Existing current ScanMXF producer is independently stat Unix seconds.

historicalSamples.interpretation: These values numerically equal the 1904-to-1970 epoch difference plus10h/11h. Producer/timezone history was not directly established. Never use one unconditional epoch conversion for all observed PMRs.

limitations: Static instructions only; no runtime call trace or timed scans.
No checksum or universal date conversion was identified on the inspected load/compare paths.
Bella policy is not implemented or approved by this native audit.

primarySources.scope: Primary Avid terminology and PMR-purpose sources; no production or media changes.
conclusions: Yes: the PMR File ID and Master ID labels correspond to FileMobId and MasterMobId roles. Existing native plus 17 genuine MXF identity checks establish the positional PMR mapping.
Avid uses FilemobID, original FilemobID and MasterMobID in Media Indexer documentation. Do not conflate Original FileMobID with the FileMobID field inspected in PMR.
FileMobID identifies Avid's media-file object. MasterMobID links it to its associated master/clip object; several media files can share a master.

For the 17 inspected MXFs, FileMobID matched the essence-owning SourcePackage and MasterMobID matched a MaterialPackage whose source graph reached that file. This local mapping should not be generalized to all MXF/AAF object arrangements.
The two IDs are binary identifiers, not UTF-8 text. Current v8/v16 representations are 32-byte AAF MobIDs; older base layouts store 8-byte OMF IDs.

The public Avid PMR KB's timestamp comparison is media-directory timestamp versus an internal directory cache entry. It does not establish the purpose of the per-record DTM field. Native tracing must settle that separately.

primarySources.title: Avid Interplay What's New for Version 2.6
primarySources.retrieval: Full PDF opened and relevant lines inspected
findings: Printed page49 lists the three identification values shown for media files in Storage Browser.
Printed page57 describes file mobs as media file information objects that can be associated with a master clip or rendered effect.

Printed page57 describes lost master mobs as assets such as sequences, master clips and subclips; this is Interplay terminology and not a declaration that every PMR second ID represents all those classes.

primarySources.title: Avid CTMS Resource pa:asset-medias
primarySources.quote: For Avid assets, this is usually the file MOB ID.

Example has one masterclip asset with three filemob entries: V1, A1 and A2. Supports explaining separate file IDs under a shared master.

primarySources.title: Avid Media Database files (msFMID.pmr and msmMMOB.mdb)
primarySources.retrieval: Canonical direct open returned internal error; indexed full article body retrieved through search.
findings: Describes PMR as a quickly loaded index of file MOBs and associated media files, used to determine online status.
Describes media-directory timestamp checks against internal PMR-cache directory timestamps, followed by reloading that directory's PMR when needed.
This directory-cache timestamp is separate from each record's DTM.

liveRecheck.scope: Read-only PMR content-hash and physical file mtime recheck against original inspected snapshot. Each file counted once using its version-16 set.

currentMediaMuster.pmrRawRead: src/mediaengine/pmrreader.cpp:305 reads ModificationWord as quint32; no epoch/timezone selected.
currentMediaMuster.projection: src/mediaengine/pmrprojection.cpp:40-59 records read status and unsupported interpretation; does not supply a timestamp or retain raw DTM in normal final rows.
currentMediaMuster.duringScanChecks: src/mediaengine/scancoordinator.cpp:282-302 compares live filesystem lastModified with discovery snapshot; src/mediaengine/scancoordinator.cpp:684 distinguishes scan stability from database freshness.
currentMediaMuster.operationChecks: src/opscanreceipt.cpp:135,144; src/oprunner.cpp:765-770; src/opfile.cpp:145-151 check actual identity, size and filesystem modification time. No PMR DTM dependency found.

limitations: The native timestamp comparisons are not all fed by a normalized Unix UTC value; the directory-entry producer has local-time conversion paths.
The historical 1904-plus-timezone interpretation is numerical evidence, not recovered historical source history.
No runtime private APIs, controlled media changes, timed scans or Windows producer tracing were used.

bellaDecision.userInstruction: No need for the modification value/date at all. The new Bella scanner and related parsers should ignore it.
bellaDecision.parsing: Skip the four-byte PMR DTM field with normal bounds checks to keep the next record aligned.
excluded: Comparing PMR DTM with filesystem time
Triggering further scanning from PMR DTM
bellaDecision.scope: PMR per-media-record DTM. Filesystem dates and operation stamps are separate physical-file facts.

bellaIdProposal.status: Complete-ID reading and duplicate/KelpieId rules subsequently approved; storage details, source precedence and header-read policy are not chosen here.
bellaIdProposal.read: Complete binary FileMobId and MasterMobId from selected PMR set; 32-byte v8/v16, 8-byte earlier-base IDs; v1 stores no master ID.
bellaIdProposal.normalize: Normalize actual source layout and numeric byte order into a consistent full-ID form; use established Avid legacy wrapper; never text-decode or truncate IDs.
bellaIdProposal.physicalAssociation: Recorded filename within the PMR media directory associates an entry with a discovered physical file. IDs then connect eligible metadata sources.
bellaIdProposal.fileMobIdUse: File-owned metadata joins within the scanner/parser. The existing Bin Filter system remains unchanged and outside Bella.
bellaIdProposal.masterMobIdUse: Associated master-owned metadata, subject to existing selected-master/source policy; no Bin Filter behavior is changed by Bella.
bellaIdProposal.inventory: Keep every supported physical media file independently of missing IDs; retain copies and related tracks as separate physical rows even when IDs repeat.
bellaIdProposal.storageProposal: Compact binary ID storage with readable formatting at display/export boundaries; not implemented or approved.
bellaIdProposal.implementationCheck: Current canonicalDatabaseId helper passes 32-byte bytes unchanged, while native AAF reader parses numeric material fields through endian-aware scalar reads. Verify big-endian 32-byte PMR normalization when implementing; genuine inspected files are little-endian.

approvedBellaIdentityRules.fullIds: Read complete FileMobId and MasterMobId, not only an eight-byte excerpt of modern IDs. Respect complete legacy representations when falling back.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.kelpieId: Retain current internal MediaMuster scan-session row identifier, independent of Avid IDs.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathAndSameFileMobId: Ignore duplicate inventory entry; keep existing row and KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.differentPathAndSameFileMobId: Keep each row with its own unique KelpieId.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.scope: Inventory row duplication; eligible metadata may still enrich the kept row. No new cross-scan persistence specified.
approvedBellaIdentityRules.samePathConflictingFileMobIds: For release one, the user explicitly assumes this cannot happen. Do not add conflict-handling machinery.

binFilterScopeClarification.status: User scope clarification; existing Bin Filter system remains unchanged
binFilterScopeClarification.userInstruction: This scope is for the Scanner/parser system. We are leaving the Bin Filter system alone, just confirmed that MDVX also uses FileMobId to filter Bins.
binFilterScopeClarification.scope: Bella replaces the scanner/parser system only. The Bin Filter system is outside Bella and remains unchanged; no new bin algorithm, matching or per-row behavior is required.
binFilterScopeClarification.comparisonConfirmed: The inspected MDVx bin filtering uses FileMobId identity; that comparison does not approve changes to MediaMuster Bin Filter behavior.

approvedBellaSetFallback.userInstruction: For now, the first release of the app: lets keep it basic and straight forward. If an entry is damaged, abandon the set and fall back to another set. How should we determine this?
approvedBellaSetFallback.damagedRecord: Any damaged record makes its entire set unusable; do not salvage individual records or combine metadata from the two sets.
approvedBellaSetFallback.setSelection: Prefer a usable version-16 set. If it is missing or unusable, use the older set only if that whole set is usable.
approvedBellaSetFallback.neitherUsable: Use no PMR metadata when neither set is usable. Keep the physical media-file inventory independently.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationStatus: User-approved release-one damage and usability checks on 18 October 2026; not implemented.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationApproval: OK, let's lock those checks in for Bella.

approvedChecks.completeEntry: Every declared record must contain all bytes required by its supported version: complete IDs, length words and counted text payloads, and the four bounded skipped modification bytes. A short record makes its whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.lengthsAndCounts: Stored text lengths and record counts must fit the available data; an overrun or impossible count makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.version16Filename: Require the verified v16 filename framing and strict UTF-8. Its two reserved prefix bytes must be present and the first zero; the native PMR helper does not constrain the second. Invalid framing or UTF-8 makes the whole set unusable.
approvedChecks.emptyFilename: An empty or null Filename makes the whole set unusable because it cannot associate that entry with a physical file. This is a Bella usability rule, not proof of structural corruption.
approvedChecks.emptySet: A set with no entries supplies no usable PMR metadata; fall back to the other usable set.

notDamage: Fields legitimately absent in older versions, including v1 Project and MasterMobId
Different entry counts between the older and version-16 sets
A database reference to a physical file that has since disappeared
approvedBellaSetFallback.safeVersion16Location: The older set physically precedes v16. Follow its lengths and counts safely to locate v16; if damaged framing makes that boundary unknowable, ignore PMR metadata rather than search for a plausible version word. Keep physical inventory.
approvedBellaSetFallback.validationLimit: These checks cannot detect every incorrect value with a valid representation. MacRoman accepts every byte, so successful decoding does not prove a Project character is correct. Ignored modification values are not inspected for semantic validity.
